title: Professions, Articles & Clear Sentences
subtitle: B1 practice with profession vocabulary, sentence construction and articles.
lessonNotes: Review profession vocabulary and use it in clear sentences.
Review a, an, the and no article before the next lesson.
Practise listening for job words, skills and responsibilities.

grammar.title: A and an
grammar.rule: Use a or an for one singular profession.

grammar.title: The
grammar.rule: Use the for a specific person or job that is already clear.

grammar.title: No article
grammar.rule: Use no article for professions in general in the plural.

grammar.title: Clear sentences
grammar.rule: Use a subject, a correct verb and useful information about duties or place.

vocabulary.meaning: a person who designs or repairs systems
a person who works with medicine
a person who writes news stories
a person who repairs water pipes
a person who cares for teeth

reading.title: A Day at the Careers Fair
reading.text: Students speak to professionals, learn what different jobs involve and write sentences about work they find interesting.

listening.title: You’re Hired: Episode 03 (B1)
listening.instructions: Watch the interview-preparation episode. Listen first for the main purpose, then note job words, skills and responsibilities.
listening.script: Use the linked activity's video and exercises before answering the strategy questions.

questions.q: On a second listen, note skills and responsibilities.

writing: Write 90–120 words about a profession you find interesting. Use a, an, the and no article correctly.
Write five clear sentences about five different professions.
Write a short careers-fair dialogue with questions and answers about work.
